pr_body:
This formats the result of the `fields` section of the `_search` API for
runtime `geo_point` fields using the `format` parameter like we do for
non-runtime `geo_point` fields. This changes the default format for
those fields from `lat, lon` to `geojson` with the option to get `wkt`
or any other format we support.

The fix does so by introducing a new method to `DocValueFormat` that
formats `GeoPoint` objects. It doesn't implement a properly serializable
`DocValueFormat` for `GeoPoint`s because one isn't required at this
point, but I don't see why we couldn't do that later on when we need
one.

Closes #85245
pr_comment: The test failure is because we had a test for fetching runtime geo points in yaml testing the bad format. Actually, we have two! #85452 tracks that.

> The test failure is because we had a test for fetching runtime geo points in yaml testing the bad format. Actually, we have two! #85452 tracks that.

I opened #85453 which I'd like to resolve before we merge this.

I was hoping to be able to access the emit values directly instead of using doc values. The reason is that doc values lose precision and it has been reported here: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/85253.  Maybe it is just a limitation / how it works.

On the other hand not being able to access emit values might make other implementations difficult. For example if we are ever going to implement geo_shape runtime fields, then we need to ba able to access the emit values as the doc values loose the information of the original data.

The precision loss you've linked sounds more like it's caused by us using `double` instead of arbitrary precision for the parsing. I think that's the precision that runtime fields have. I could be wrong though.

> The precision loss you've linked sounds more like it's caused by us using `double` instead of arbitrary precision for the parsing. I think that's the precision that runtime fields have. I could be wrong though.

I just talked with @iverase. Going through doc values adds an encoding step which pitches even more precision than regular old double precision floating point. So I'll rework this not to go through doc values.
Hi @nik9000, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> Can this be considered a breaking change?

I admit to being a bit hazy still, but I've been considering this a bug. We'd intended runtime geo_points to have the same defaults as regular geo_points.
But it totally could be considered breaking.

> LGTM

For those following along at home I had a conversation with a few folks directly how this breaks and convinced them to consider this a bug fix. It does change the default format for *runtime* geo_point fields. But it changes it to be the same as regular geo_point fields. Which feels like we're fixing a bug. To me.

> I think it is ok to use the approach you use for the distance feature query. We can switch on a follow up PR but if you want to implement it is ok too. Just make sure you encode /decode values so they match the values on an index.

I'd prefer if you grabbed that one, yeah. Thanks so much!
